title: Formal glueing: Can is an equivalence of R-modules with glueing data
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $f_1,\dots,f_t\in R$, and let $\mathrm{Glue}=\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\dots,f_t)$ be the category of glueing data, with the canonical maps $c^P_f:(P\otimes_RS)_f\to P_f\otimes_RS$ and $\sigma^P_{f,g}:(P_f)_g\to(P_g)_f$ and the localizations $P_f$, $h_f$ of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. For an $R$-module $M$ put $\mathrm{Can}(M)=(M\otimes_RS,(M_{f_i})_i,(c^M_{f_i})_i,(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j})_{i,j})$, and for an $R$-linear map $u:M\to N$ put $\mathrm{Can}(u)=(u\otimes_RS,(u_{f_i})_i)$ [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].
(1) For every $R$-module $P$ and $f,g\in R$ the maps $c^P_f$ and $\sigma^P_{f,g}$ are isomorphisms; $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ is an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$, $\mathrm{Can}(u)$ is a morphism $\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$, and $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}$ is a functor.
(2) Assume moreover that $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that, for the ideal $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$, the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. Then $\mathrm{Can}$ is an equivalence of categories: it is fully faithful (for $R$-modules $M,N$, every morphism $\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ in $\mathrm{Glue}$ equals $\mathrm{Can}(u)$ for exactly one $R$-linear $u:M\to N$) and essentially surjective (every object of $\mathrm{Glue}$ is isomorphic in $\mathrm{Glue}$ to $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ for some $R$-module $M$).

proof.text: Comparison is bijective by compare_properties. The two identities for swap and reverse swap in swap_properties give injectivity and surjectivity directly.
Obtain the prescribed canonical functor and its object and morphism equalities from lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-functor.

Under flatness and the quotient isomorphism, equality of Can.map a and Can.map b gives HEq of their prime and chart maps. Transport using hmap and apply eq_of_heq to get equality of the actual base changes and localizations. Evaluate these at 1 tensor m and m/1. Their images under the initial map of the formal glueing complex agree, so its injectivity gives a(m)=b(m). Extensionality gives a=b.
The morphism-lifting lemma gives surjectivity of each Can.map. Combine with the preceding injectivity to get bijectivity on every Hom set.
For this same functor, apply the algebraization lemma to each datum X, giving the required module and isomorphism. Combine the clauses, retaining all prescribed object and map equations.

theorem exists_canonical_equivalence {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R) :
    (∀ (P : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (a b : R),
      Function.Bijective (compare φ a P) ∧ Function.Bijective (swap a b P)) ∧
    ∃ Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f,
      (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))) ∧
      (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (h : M ⟶ N),
        HEq (Can.map h).prime (extendMap φ h.hom) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.map h).chart i) (localMap (f i) h.hom)) ∧
      (φ.Flat →
        Function.Bijective
          (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map) →
        (∀ M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
          Function.Bijective (Can.map : (M ⟶ N) → (Can.obj M ⟶ Can.obj N))) ∧
        (∀ X : Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f,
          ∃ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R, Nonempty (Can.obj M ≅ X)))
lean.note: The existential functor is specified on every object and morphism by equalities of bundled modules and HEq of linear maps, avoiding any choice of unproved data in a definition. The final conditional asserts bijectivity of all Hom maps and essential surjectivity for this same functor.
